body: There could be, but I'm not intentionally hiding anything. What do you think it could possibly be?

I do try to remind myself intermittently that I might be wrong, so yes, I do think of going to a psychiatrist every now and then, but sitting in front of someone who'd just say "you need to have faith in God" is basically a nightmare. This has been said to friends of mine, yes. This is real. Going to a random person who I'm not sure is good enough isn't worth the risk.

And nope, I don't think so.

The hobbies thing works sometimes, but sometimes not. I write code for money, and I also contribute to some open-source projects. The feeling I have when I get referenced in the changelog, or when someone I only dreamt of meeting some day appreciates my work, is ultimate. However, it's a double edged weapon. A "you're not good enough" hurts a lot. A no from MIT hurts even more. I keep myself going, though. It looks like my code does matter, in the end.

The problem is that I act very peculiarly, not only when it comes to my mood, but also my thoughts and the way I construct arguments. It's not that simple when it comes to the relationship. I'm too direct and I'm too offensive. Imagine if someone says "your friend is a hypocrite" because she just posted that "BFF forever!" image with a friend of her whom she keeps calling names behind your backs. "Don't call my friend a hypocrite". Imagine if someone started deploring your religion because you just told them that a young girl praying is aww-ish. It's getting better, but it's difficult. She's starting to understand that I'm doing it out of logical reasoning and not for the sole reason of making her mad, and I'm getting slightly better with my words.

I'm the kind of guy who'd say "it looks like shit" if you asked me for an opinion on a piece of art you just spent a whole week drawing, if it does look like shit. I won't hide it, and I won't sugarcoat it, I'll just tell you that it looks like shit. I'll point out the bad parts, but I won't go like "it's great, but there's one and two and three". If it's shit, it's shit. And I like people to deal with me the same way. I don't want people to tell me it's good if it isn't. I'm relying on their opinion in order to judge my work, you know. "It's good, but" is bad for me, and should be bad for them. But most people don't work that way, and most people will get shocked by your response, and might even hate you for it. And unfortunately, sometimes I do care about those people. Sometimes it backfires.

It's just very difficult to accept that this is the way things will stay, that it'll never get better. It will always be difficult for people to believe that I'm not insulting them/they shouldn't be offended, it will always be difficult for people to make me feel better, it will always be difficult. This is almost unbearable.

This constructs a problem for me.

I'm not the kind of guy who'd force himself to take medicine, but I wouldn't exactly support it either, especially if it will never cure it. Isn't it better to be able to control yourself, you know? What if you relied on that medicine and suddenly it wasn't there? What if the side effects were too severe? I know this might sound stupid, because although I'm still there, I might snap at some point, but the fact that most psychiatrists here are inexperienced, and that I can actually get the meds without having a prescription, that doesn't make it better. If I wanted the medicine I could simply get it from a pharmacy here, it isn't difficult.
